verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO verifier reported binary_reward 0 with continuous reward 0.602 and opt_commit false [1], and passing requires reward strictly above 1.2 on the gm_speedup_patch_commit metric [2]. The task asked to optimize `maybe_sequence_to_range` for the shown random-integer benchmark while keeping results functionally equivalent and pursuing the best possible speedup [3]. The hidden reference commit bfaf917 replaces the full-array `np.divmod` path with a compiled `lib.is_sequence_range` Cython helper that short-circuits on the first mismatch [4][5]. The agent initially pursued that same Cython approach but reverted it after concluding meson/ninja/cython were unavailable, then landed a pure-Python block-validation loop in `pandas/core/indexes/base.py` [6][7]. That patch preserved correctness—the verifier ran all 20 held-out tests with equivalence checks passing—but on aggregate the patched build was only ~60% as fast as the reference commit (geometric-mean commit/patch ≈ 0.602), nowhere near the 1.2 bar [1][8]. The agent's own validation focused on the instruction's random non-range case (~14.7 ms → ~5.3 µs) and did not surface the large regressions on range-shaped inputs where the block loop must scan the full sequence [9][10]. The attempt was directionally right and materially faster than baseline on test 0, but it is not the reference-quality optimization this task gates on, so TN is the right classification.
